subject: SIG: Request for network connectivity evidence (VPC peering, private endpoints, IP allowlists)
messages:
From: John Daley <john.daley@acme-corp.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 08:14:00 -0800
Subject: SIG - Network evidence request: VPC peering / private endpoints / allowlists

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for engaging with Acme on the SIG. Our security team is working through the Standardized Information Gathering questionnaire and has flagged a few follow-up items specifically around network connectivity. To complete our review we need: 

- A brief description of how Redwood handles private connectivity for hosted customers (VPC peering vs. private endpoint).
- Concrete identifiers and evidence for peering where applicable (VPC IDs, peering connection IDs, region).
- The public-facing egress IP ranges you expect customers to allow; if those are dynamic, please provide an up-to-date allowlist or the required process to obtain it.
- Example request/response headers (or traceroute) that show the source IP for a hosted private endpoint, or a sample IP to allowlist for webhooks.
- Any documented controls around routing isolation for dedicated vs. hosted customers.

If possible, can you provide the items above and any attachments (diagram, CIDR lists, peering metadata) by end of day Monday so we can circle back to our SOC/SIG reviewer? If you prefer a quick call to walk through the network diagram I can bring our infra lead.

Appreciate it — we want to keep the review moving.

John
Security Engineer
Acme Corp


From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
To: John Daley <john.daley@acme-corp.com>
Cc: security@acme-corp.com <security@acme-corp.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG - Network evidence request: VPC peering / private endpoints / allowlists

John — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Karthik from Infrastructure and Marissa from Solutions so they can assemble artifacts.

Planned next steps:
- Karthik will confirm the exact VPC/peering IDs and produce a CIDR/allowlist CSV.
- Marissa will export a short diagram and fill the SIG network answer sheet.
- I will provide a brief note describing our connectivity modes (hosted API, dedicated VPC peering, and customer-managed private endpoints) and point to the console docs.

Can you confirm whether the allowlist needs to be a single static IP per hosting region or whether a CIDR block is acceptable? That will affect how we package the response.

We should be able to get preliminary attachments to you by Monday EOD PST. If you prefer a walkthrough before that, propose a 30-min window Monday morning.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Security & Trust
Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: John Daley <john.daley@acme-corp.com>, security@acme-corp.com <security@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG - Network evidence request: VPC peering / private endpoints / allowlists

Grace / Marissa — quick technical summary and artifacts we can include: 

1) Connectivity modes (short):
- Hosted API: customers connect to the Redwood public API; customers who require private communication may use our Private offering which supports VPC peering and PrivateLink-style endpoints (AWS NLB + endpoint services).
- Dedicated: reserved capacity in customer-provisioned VPCs with explicit peering/VRF boundaries.

2) Peering metadata (examples we can include):
- Redwood hosted VPCs (us-west-2): vpc-0a1b2c3d4e (redwood-prod-usw2)
- Peering connection (example): pcx-0f1e2d3c4b5a6 (established 2026-08-10)
- For Dedicated customers we provide a per-customer peering record; we will redact tenant IDs but can provide the connection ID and region so Acme can confirm topology.

3) Egress/allowlist guidance:
- Stable egress IP ranges: we publish consolidated NAT egress CIDRs per region; for us-west-2 the current set is 34.200.0.0/16, 3.110.0.0/16 (these are example ranges — we'll export the live list).
- If Acme prefers single IPs for webhook allowlists, we can provide a small set of stable NAT IPs upon request for the given region. For high assurance we recommend CIDR allowlists plus short-term IPs for debugging.

4) Evidence we will attach:
- redwood-vpc-peering-summary.xlsx (sheet with VPC IDs, peering IDs, region, creation dates)
- ip-allowlist-sample.csv (current published egress CIDRs by region)
- sig-network-answer-sheet.pdf (filled answers for the SIG about routing isolation and controls)

Open questions for Acme:
- Do you need traceroute-level evidence (we can capture a sample traceroute from a private endpoint) or is a documented example IP sufficient?
- For Dedicated customers, do you require tenant-scoped flow logs as evidence (we can provide process notes; actual logs are customer-specific)?

We'll prepare the attachments and the SIG answer sheet now.

— Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: John Daley <john.daley@acme-corp.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 09:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG - Network evidence request: VPC peering / private endpoints / allowlists

John — attaching the consolidated package for your reviewer. Contents:

- sig-network-answer-sheet.pdf (filled answers for SIG questions on network segregation, private endpoints, and peering controls)
- redwood-vpc-peering-summary.xlsx (table of example peering records; customer-specific IDs are redacted where required)
- ip-allowlist-sample.csv (published egress CIDRs by region and a small set of stable NAT IPs for troubleshooting)

Attachment notes: we have redacted tenant-identifying tags in the peering spreadsheet; if Acme requires full tenant-scoped records we can provide them under an NDA. The ip-allowlist-sample.csv includes both CIDRs and three sample NAT egress IPs per region suitable for webhook allowlisting.

If helpful, I can run a 30-min walkthrough Monday at 9am PST to show the diagram and answer any questions. Otherwise please confirm the files suffice and which format you prefer for traceroute evidence (raw traceroute output vs. annotated diagram).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: sig-network-answer-sheet.pdf, redwood-vpc-peering-summary.xlsx, ip-allowlist-sample.csv

From: security@acme-corp.com <security@acme-corp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 11:37:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG - Network evidence request: VPC peering / private endpoints / allowlists

Marissa / team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the artifacts. Our reviewer had a couple final clarifying asks before closing the SIG: 

1) Please confirm whether the "stable NAT IPs" listed are advertised from a single ASN or through multiple egress points; we need to provide this to our network ops team so they can implement BGP-based filters if required.

2) For the peering IDs you provided, can you share the CloudTrail-style event snippet (time/actor/action) showing the peering establishment (redacted actor ok) — that helps our auditor verify the change control process.

3) We'll take the CIDRs for allowlisting; if you can also provide one sample traceroute from a Private endpoint to a test webhook URL (showing source IP) that will let us confirm path and NAT behaviour.

If you can provide the three items above by COB Monday we'll mark the network section as resolved. If it's easier to run the 9am PST walkthrough, please send a meeting invite and we'll bring our network ops lead.

Best,
Acme Security Team
